name: CHAI Incubator threshold analysis BOTEC
summary: Funds CHAI's incubator, which develops new health programs for possible future funding. GiveWell's spreadsheet "CHAI Incubator threshold analysis BOTEC", linked from its grant page. Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values.

resources.title: GiveWell grant page (Clinton Health Access Initiative Incubator August 2022)

rows.label: How long we fund opportunities incubated by CHAI (years) (Conservative)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's input behind the present value, read from the sheet so the present value moves with your discount rate.

rows.label: How fast these opportunities get worse each year
rows.explainer: GiveWell's assumption that the cost-effectiveness of funding opportunities falls by 5% a year; it is not time preference, so the discount slider leaves it alone.

rows.label: Discount rate on future benefits (time preference)
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. GiveWell's sheet lowers later years only by how fast these opportunities get worse (its own rate, kept), not for time: a benefit in a later year otherwise counts as much as one now. The site discounts every future benefit at one shared rate (Next year's good counts less by, under Your values), applied on top of the sheet's rate. The evaluator view keeps only the sheet's rate.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar from CHAI grant per year (Conservative)
rows.explainer: Calculated in the source sheet as `=(B16-B17)/(B4*1000000)`; kept as a fixed number here, as the yearly amount the present value below discounts.

rows.label: Present discounted value of additional units of value per dollar (Conservative)
rows.explainer:
GiveWell's `=pv(B18,B12,-B19,,1)`, rebuilt from the sheet's own inputs so the present value moves with your discount rate.

Calculation

rows.label: Units of value per dollar, GiveDirectly (Conservative)
rows.explainer: Top charities cost-effectiveness analysis. Changed for consistency: GiveWell's sheet used 0.00344 units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly here. The site values cash with one shared benchmark for every model (The cash benchmark, under Data), the same figure that turns this model's multiple of cash back into units of value: where the sheet divides by it to make its multiple, the benchmark cancels in our view, so our units of value are the sheet's before it divided by cash. The evaluator view keeps 0.00344.

rows.label: Expected cost-effectiveness of this grant (x cash) (Conservative)
Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years. It is the site's shared cash benchmark (The cash benchmark, under Data), the one figure every model's multiple of cash is turned into units of value with.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
